item.title: Hong Kong court overturns fraud conviction for pro-democracy activist Jimmy Lai
item.description: A Hong Kong appeals court on Thursday overturned Jimmy Lai’s 2022 fraud conviction and sentencing in a rare legal victory for the pro-democracy activist.

item.title: Minneapolis woman who Ilhan Omar took to State of the Union needed medical care after arrest
item.description: Omar said Capitol Police "aggressively handled" her guest, Aliyah Rahman of Minneapolis, forcing her to seek medical care at a hospital.

item.title: Former Prince Andrew's arrest is a ‘first step,’ Virginia Giuffre's family says
item.description: The family of the Virginia Roberts Giuffre is speaking out after former Prince Andrew was arrested over his ties to Jeffrey Epstein. Speaking to NBC News’ Hallie Jackson, Giuffre's brother, Sky Roberts, said it was a “first step” toward justice for his sister.

item.title: FBI raids properties of Los Angeles schools chief
item.description: The FBI is raiding properties belonging to LAUSD superintendent Alberto Carvalho. No arrests were made in the operation and the reason for the major search is still unknown. NBC News’ Camila Bernal has the latest.

item.title: Heart disease and stroke are the No. 1 killers of women. Even younger women could be at risk.
item.description: Without better prevention and early detection, the number of women living with cardiovascular disease will increase substantially in the next 25 years, the American Heart Association said.

item.title: Trump said Iran will 'soon' have missiles able to hit the U.S. A 2025 intel report said it will take 10 years.
item.description: President Trump said Iran is working to build missiles that could "soon" strike America. U.S. intelligence reports have offered a more cautious view.

item.title: Investigators return to Nancy Guthrie’s home
item.description: One day after the Guthrie family offered a $1,000,000 reward for information leading to their mother’s return, there was a surge in law enforcement activity at her Arizona home. NBC News’ Liz Kreutz reports.

item.title: Vance announces pause of Medicaid payments to Minnesota
item.description: Vance announces pause of Medicaid payments to Minnesota

item.title: New questions over Epstein documents which have not been released by DOJ
item.description: The Justice Department has not released summaries and notes from some FBI interviews with a woman who alleges she was sexually assaulted by both Jeffrey Epstein and President Trump, according to an NBC News analysis and information provided by a source familiar with the investigation. NBC News’ Hallie Jackson reports.

item.title: Cuba says 4 people killed after gunfight with Florida speedboat
item.description: Cuba’s Interior Ministry said passengers on a speedboat registered in Florida opened fire on its border patrol agents, who returned fire and killed four people. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said the U.S. will conduct an independent investigation. NBC News’ Jose Diaz-Balart reports.
